obligation: CPNI breach notice to law enforcement (current rule)
trigger: Reasonable determination that a person, without or exceeding authorization, intentionally gained access to, used, or disclosed CPNI (64.2011(e)); in the P08 scenario, confirmed export of call detail records from the voice platform
deadline: As soon as practicable and no later than 7 business days after reasonable determination (internal target: 2 business days)
notify: USSS and FBI electronically through the FCC central reporting facility (link at fcc.gov/eb/cpni)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - interconnected VoIP provider (64.2003(o)); no size exemption

obligation: CPNI breach: hold on customer and public notice
trigger: Law enforcement notice filed
deadline: No customer or public disclosure until 7 full business days after the USSS and FBI notice, notwithstanding contrary state law. Earlier notice only if the company flags an extraordinarily urgent need and consults the investigating agency; the agency may direct a delay of up to 30 days, extendable, in writing
notify: Hold; keep any agency direction (the agency logs it on the reporting facility)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: CPNI breach notice to customers (current rule)
trigger: Law enforcement notice process complete
deadline: After the hold ends (or as the agency directs). The current rule sets no further outer deadline, so plan to the Florida 30-day clock below
notify: Each customer whose CPNI was breached (in the scenario, about 390 voice accounts)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

trigger: Any CPNI breach discovered
deadline: Record kept at least 2 years: dates of discovery and notices, detailed description of the CPNI, circumstances
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: CPNI and covered data breach notice (2023 amendments; NOT yet effective)
citation: 47 CFR 64.2011 as amended by FCC 23-111 (89 FR 9968); upheld in Ohio Telecom Ass'n v. FCC (6th Cir. 2025-08-13)
trigger: Would cover inadvertent as well as intentional access, and customer PII (for example, driver license numbers) as well as CPNI
deadline: Would require FCC, USSS, and FBI notice within 7 business days; customer notice without unreasonable delay and within 30 days after reasonable determination; breaches under 500 customers with no reasonably likely harm reported in an annual summary
applies_at_this_tier: No - amendments to 64.2011 remain delayed indefinitely; no FCC effective-date notice in the Federal Register through 2026-10-05. Recheck at the start of every incident

trigger: Any compromise of a lawful interception or of call-identifying information to unauthorized persons, or any unlawful electronic surveillance on company premises
deadline: Within a reasonable time upon discovery
notify: Affected law enforcement agencies (through the TTP and the agency contacts in the intercept record)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the voice platform intercept function, TTP equipment, or intercept records were reached or cannot be ruled out

trigger: Outage that potentially affects a 911 special facility as defined in 4.5(e) (for this company, mainly a loss of 911 calling across its numbers long enough to reach 900,000 user minutes; the company also calls the 911 center as a courtesy for any 911 outage over 30 minutes)
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 minutes after discovery, by telephone and in writing electronically; first follow-up no later than 2 hours after initial contact
notify: Designated outage contacts at the county 911 center (confirmed annually, 4.9(h)(1))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - wireline and interconnected VoIP provider

trigger: Wireline outage of at least 30 minutes that affects at least 667 OC3 minutes (for example, the edge router or middle-mile circuit taken down during containment: about 64 OC3 equivalents x 30 minutes = about 1,920), or meets the other 4.9(f) tests
deadline: Notification within 120 minutes of discovery; Initial Communications Outage Report within 72 hours; Final Communications Outage Report within 30 days
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - thresholds are outage-based, not size-based

trigger: VoIP outage of at least 30 minutes that potentially affects a 911 or 988 special facility; or 900,000 user minutes with complete loss of service; or special offices and facilities
deadline: Notification within 240 minutes (911 or 988 facility affected) or 24 hours (other triggers); Final Communications Outage Report within 30 days
applies_at_this_tier: Yes, but the user-minute test needs about 34 hours of total loss across 440 numbers

trigger: FCC activates DIRS for the county (for example, a hurricane during the incident)
deadline: Daily infrastructure status reports from activation until deactivation; timely DIRS reports replace NORS for outages in the activated area
applies_at_this_tier: Yes when activated (facilities-based wireline provider)

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents. In the scenario, names with driver license numbers (about 1,050 accounts) read through the BSS API key. Call detail alone may not be Florida-defined personal information; counsel decides
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred, unless a law enforcement agency requests a delay in writing (501.171(4)(b)). Coordinate with the CPNI hold: counsel sends one combined notice after the hold ends and inside the 30 days
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to notice to individuals, not to this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 1,050 individuals in the scenario

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 1,050 individuals in the scenario

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice (inbound from vendors)
trigger: A vendor that maintains personal information for the company (BSS vendor, voice platform provider, answering service) has a breach
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the vendor's determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - add to vendor contracts (POAM-011)

trigger: Affected individuals whose residence is outside Florida (all service addresses are in Florida, but some billing addresses are not)
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check the billing address of every affected individual; apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom or extortion payment (for example, a demand not to publish stolen call records)
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement (FBI) or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (pending final rule)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Statute: 72 hours (covered incident); 24 hours (ransom payment). Not yet effective
applies_at_this_tier: No - no final rule in the Federal Register as of 2026-10-05; the proposed Communications sector criterion names VoIP and internet service providers. Voluntary report to CISA and FBI on day 0-2 instead

trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at a public registrant
deadline: 4 business days after materiality determination
applies_at_this_tier: No - privately held

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article from Kaspersky Lab
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

citation: Customer contracts (6 dedicated circuits, including the town hall and the community bank branch)
trigger: Security incident or outage affecting the customer's service or data
deadline: Per contract; outage credits under the 99.9% commitment. Any CPNI breach notice to these customers still waits for the 64.2011(b) hold unless the agency agrees
notify: Customer contract contacts (Owner and General Manager calls)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not regulatory

trigger: Suspected security incident, extortion demand, or data theft
deadline: Per policy: prompt notice through the 24x7 breach hotline, before hiring outside firms; use panel counsel and forensics
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not regulatory
